auditLog.title: Audit Log
auditLog.retentionNote: Logs are kept for 30 days and then purged automatically every day
auditLog.purgeConfirm: This will permanently delete all audit log entries older than 30 days. Continue?

points: Create a "Cash Box" account and a "Bank" account if you have one, and set the opening balance to the exact cash you actually hold today.
One account is enough for both sales and purchases - no need for a separate account per movement type. The "Source" column in the transaction log already shows the type of each movement.
Click the "Transaction Log" 📖 icon next to any account to see all its movements, with search, pagination, and print/export-to-Excel buttons.

The "Reconciled" column in the transaction log: only check it for a movement you've actually confirmed from a bank statement or cash count, so "book balance" can be compared against "reconciled balance".
Use "Transfer Between Accounts" to move money between the cash box and bank, and "Record Capital Movement" to add/withdraw personal capital.
The "Due Date" field on sales/purchase invoices is optional - if you give customers a payment grace period (30 days, say), fill it in so the aging here stays accurate.
The four columns (0-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / over 90 days) split the same "remaining" amount by debt age - they always add up to the "remaining" total.
Pay special attention to the "over 90 days" column - that's the money most at risk of being forgotten or lost.
There's a search box by customer/supplier name and pagination if you have a lot of parties.
Record any check you receive from a customer or issue to a supplier, with its number, bank name, and due date.
When the check actually clears, click "Clear Check" and pick the account - it's automatically reflected in that account's balance.
If a check bounces, mark it "Bounced" instead of deleting it - it stays in the historical record.

fiscalClosing.warning: This action cannot be undone: after closing, you won't be able to record or edit any financial transaction, complete a stocktake, or edit/cancel/return any sales or purchase invoice dated on or before the closing date.
points: Only use this after you're sure you've finished all your entries for a given period (month/year end).
The goal: protect your closed figures (e.g. ones already submitted externally) from being accidentally changed later.
For tracking things like a delivery vehicle or equipment - fill in the cost, purchase date, and useful life in months.
If you paid for it from an account, select it - it's deducted automatically and shows up in the cash flow statement as "Investing".
"Accumulated Depreciation" and "Net Book Value" update automatically every month with no action needed from you.
When you sell or dispose of the asset, click "Dispose Asset" 🏷️.
A snapshot (right now) of everything you own (cash+bank, inventory, receivables, fixed assets) against what you owe (payables) and your equity.
Review it monthly to keep an overall eye on the shop's financial health.
Splits cash movement for the chosen period into 3 activity types: Operating (sales/purchases/expenses), Investing (buying/selling fixed assets), Financing (capital).
The closing balance at the end should always match the total of your actual account balances on the "Accounts" screen.

stocktake.warning: Completing a stocktake is final - it applies the differences directly to real stock and cannot be undone or edited afterward.
points: Click "New Stocktake" and pick a warehouse - the system pulls in all products and their system quantities automatically.
Count the actual goods and record the real quantity for each item - the difference is calculated instantly.
Click "Complete Stocktake" only after you've double-checked every number.

shortages.title: Driver Shortages
shortages.pricingHint: Used to value any shortage in this count
shortages.confirmReopen: The shortage will return to pending; a cash payment entry will be removed. Continue?
shortages.recordedHint: The shortage was recorded against the driver - settle it from the "Driver Shortages" tab.
guide: Every van count with missing goods is recorded here against the van's driver, priced as chosen at count time (sale or cost).
Settle by deducting from a month's salary (shown on the Employees screen), cash payment (goes to the cash box), or waiving with a reason.
Click a driver's card to see only their shortages. A wrong settlement can be reopened.
Waived shortages count as a loss at cost and reduce profit; shortages deducted from salary or paid in cash are recovered and are not a loss.

loadRequests.title: Load Requests
guide: Drivers send load requests from "My Van" (usually for tomorrow) and you get a notification.
On approval pick the warehouse and adjust quantities; a real load voucher is created and goods move to the van.
When rejecting, write the reason so the driver sees it.
